name: Winna

signupBonus.headline: No deposit-match bonus — instead up to 60% rakeback through the VIP Club, with 5% unlocked instantly once you cross $1,000 in cumulative wagers
signupBonus.detail: Rakeback is paid automatically roughly every seven minutes and carries no additional wagering requirement once earned. Winna's welcome offer is a 1x wagering requirement on deposited funds before withdrawal — low compared with the 30x-40x common on a traditional deposit-match bonus, though also a lower bar since there's no bonus balance to unlock in the first place. There is no promo code or referral-code deposit match; the whole model runs on rakeback rather than a locked bonus.

editorial.summary:
Winna is a young crypto casino, sportsbook and prediction-market platform — live since summer 2024, operated by GG Gaming S.R.L. out of Costa Rica under a supplementary Tobique Gaming Commission licence issued through the Tobique First Nation in New Brunswick, Canada. It scaled unusually fast for a new entrant, closing a $15 million seed round within months of launch, and the product reflects that ambition: 6,000+ slot and table titles, live dealer tables from Evolution, Pragmatic Play, Microgaming and BGaming, a 30-plus-sport sportsbook, and — the feature that gets it listed on this page separately from most casinos here — a prediction-markets section covering elections, corporate leadership changes, company performance and even awards like the Nobel Prize, alongside the sports contracts you'd expect.

We need to lead with the most serious thing we found rather than bury it under the game count. Multiple independent reviewers and a recurring pattern of player complaints describe Winna adjusting the outcomes of its own in-house Originals games — not just complaint volume about bad luck, but specific, repeated allegations that the platform lowered the probability of large multipliers and, separately, reduced the payout value on hits that did land, with one commonly cited example describing a win cut from roughly 1000x down to about 130x. We were not able to independently verify the mechanism behind these claims — we don't have access to Winna's game code or RNG audit logs — but the allegation is specific, appears across multiple unconnected sources rather than a single aggrieved poster, and describes exactly the kind of harm a "provably fair" claim is supposed to make impossible. That tension between the marketing claim and the complaint pattern is the central fact about this casino, and we think you should weigh it before the bonus terms.

Separately, and consistent with a young, fast-growing operator: withdrawal delays are a recurring theme, with some player reports describing 36 to 50 days between a requested withdrawal and payment, and new verification requests appearing after an account was already approved — a pattern that reads as re-review rather than a one-time check. Roughly 41% of Trustpilot reviewers leave one star, citing withheld winnings and what they describe as rigged outcomes; a large share of the remaining reviews are genuinely enthusiastic about fast payouts and VIP support, and the two pictures coexist rather than one cancelling the other out.

The ratings reflect that same split more starkly than almost any other casino we've reviewed: Casino Guru's Safety Index sits at a very high 9.3, while AskGamblers' player rating is a poor 3.7 with unresolved complaints over withheld winnings and changed bonus terms. A near six-point gap between two respected platforms on the same casino is unusual even by this site's standards, and we'd rather show you both numbers than average away what they disagree about.

On the KYC side, Winna advertises no-verification signup and low-friction play, and independent guides describe a real, if not universally consistent, threshold: verification is commonly triggered around €2,000 in withdrawals or on flagged activity, a bar high enough that ordinary-stakes players are unlikely to hit it in the normal course of play, which is why we're tagging it no-KYC on the same basis we use for other casinos with a stated threshold — while flagging that this is the same operator whose payout-integrity complaints are described above.
pros: A genuinely uncommon feature set: casino, sportsbook and prediction markets (elections, corporate news, awards) on one account, not just sports and slots
Low-friction bonus structure — up to 60% rakeback with only a 1x wagering requirement on deposits, rather than a locked deposit-match bonus with a steep clearing requirement
No-KYC signup with a stated ~€2,000 verification threshold, high enough that ordinary-stakes players are unlikely to trigger it in normal play
Broad crypto support (13 coins across five native chains) including multiple network options for USDT
cons: Multiple independent reviewers and a recurring player-complaint pattern allege Winna manually reduced the odds of large multipliers on its in-house Originals and cut the payout value on wins that did land — we could not independently verify the mechanism, but the allegation is specific, repeated across unconnected sources, and directly contradicts a provably fair claim

AskGamblers' player rating (3.7/10) and Casino Guru's Safety Index (9.3/10) diverge by nearly six points on the same casino — an unusually wide gap even among the casinos on this site, worth reading as a signal that the two platforms are picking up genuinely different things
Recurring withdrawal-delay complaints, with some player reports describing 36 to 50 days for payment and new verification requests appearing after an account was already approved
About 41% of Trustpilot reviewers leave one star, citing withheld winnings and rigged-outcome complaints — a heavier negative skew than most casinos on this site

Very young operator (live since mid-2024) with less accumulated track record than most other casinos on this site, and licensed through a lighter-touch Tobique First Nation framework alongside its Costa Rica registration

aiSummary.withdrawals: Independent guides describe verification as commonly triggered around €2,000 in withdrawals or on flagged activity, with reported minimum withdrawal around $20 regardless of coin and a default daily cap around $25,000 that rises with account tier. Reported processing experience is inconsistent: some players describe payouts clearing in around 10 minutes, while a recurring complaint pattern describes 36-to-50-day delays and additional verification requests appearing after an account was already approved. We were unable to reconcile these into one consistent typical figure.
aiSummary.deposits: Deposits are reported to start from $1 in any of the 13 supported coins, crediting quickly per third-party guides. We did not find independently sourced native-unit minimum figures specific enough to cite with confidence beyond the commonly repeated $1 headline figure.
aiSummary.commonProblems: The most serious recurring theme is a specific, repeated allegation that Winna's in-house Originals games had their odds and payout values manually adjusted to reduce large wins — described across multiple independent reviews and player complaints rather than a single source, and in direct tension with the platform's provably fair claim. We could not independently verify the underlying mechanism. Separately, withdrawal-delay complaints and post-approval re-verification requests recur across Trustpilot and other review sources, alongside genuinely positive reports of fast payouts and responsive VIP support from other players — both patterns are well documented and neither cancels the other out.
